Al-Murtaḍā stresses that repelling danger without intent to kill remains possible."}, {"id": "5:28/q06/p2", "position": "He will neither retaliate nor fight his brother, even if Cain attacks.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī reports Ibn ʿAbbās's refusal to retaliate; al-Zajjāj lists fighting and killing. {"id": "5:28/q07", "question": "Why would Abel refrain from defending himself?", "turns_on": "The evidence for a law against defense, a lawful personal choice, or an attack by surprise.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q07/p1", "position": "His era's law forbade resisting a would-be killer, requiring patient submission.", "reasons": "Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, al-Jubbāʾī and Ibn Jurayj report this law, with Ibn Jurayj locating it among Israelites. Al-Ṭabrisī says God would exact justice. Al-Zajjāj reports a broader ban on swords, likened to Jesus's time and Muhammad's Meccan period. Ibn ʿĀshūr infers a bar on deadly defense from Abel's fear and says later law abrogated it. Al-Nasafī adds the risk of sharing the killer's sin."}, {"id": "5:28/q07/p2", "position": "He could defend himself but chose restraint out of scruple and hope of reward.", "reasons": "Reports say he was stronger than Cain. Al-Māwardī and Ibn al-Jawzī say defense was lawful; al-Baghawī says submission could seek reward. Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers this, reasoning that Cain was a sinful monotheist, since scrupling against an unbeliever would make less sense; he compares ʿUthmān. Al-Bayḍāwī gives the better course as an alternative, al-Ālūsī the greater reward, and Ibn ʿĀshūr stresses life's sanctity even for an unjust person."}, {"id": "5:28/q07/p3", "position": "The words warned Cain before the attack; they do not establish a conscious refusal of defense when attacked.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī says no proof shows Abel knew in time and reports he was killed asleep. Al-Rāzī and Abū Ḥayyān say he spoke to deter Cain before a probable threat and was then struck with a stone in sleep. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers stealth and rejects reports of enabled murder as weak, inconsistent with Qurʾān and sound reflection; he raises complicity in sin. The Study Quran says sleep left no chance to defend."}, {"id": "5:28/q07/p4", "position": "His refusal exposed the enormity of Cain's murderous intent.", "reasons": "The Study Quran frames the commentator dispute over refusal despite an explicit threat and reports this explanation; al-Rāzī says Abel's pre-attack words admonished Cain, and Ibn ʿĀshūr says they warn of murder's gravity."}, {"id": "5:28/q07/p5", "position": "An inherited charge from Adam may have forbidden taking any life, even in defense.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr offers this as an alternative to Abel's own inference from slaughter and hunting; his own apparent reading is Abel's judgment that all life was sacred."}]}
{"id": "5:28/q08", "question": "Was Abel stronger than Cain?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q08/p1", "position": "Yes; strength made his restraint a matter of scruple rather than incapacity.", "reasons": "ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr/ʿUmar is named in variant attributions. {"id": "5:28/q09", "question": "Why use a nominal participle and emphatic bāʾ in the refusal?", "turns_on": "Whether the form chiefly marks vile identity, the first steps of murder, or restraint in claiming future certainty.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q09/p1", "position": "They emphatically deny that Abel would acquire the shameful character of a killer.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Rāzī, al-Bayḍāwī and al-Samīn contrast the verbal condition with its nominal response; the bāʾ strengthens negation. Abū Ḥayyān transmits al-Zamakhsharī; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī adds the oath."}, {"id": "5:28/q09/p2", "position": "It disavows even the acts leading toward murder.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī says rejecting the stretch of the hand is stronger than merely denying the completed killing."}, {"id": "5:28/q09/p3", "position": "It emphasizes his present refusal while reverently avoiding a certain claim about future conduct.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī connects the nominal expression and emphatic negation with reverence toward God."}]}

{"id": "5:28/q11", "question": "Why does Abel say he fears God?", "turns_on": "The notes distinguish fear as restraint, a sign of knowledge, and the causal explanation of the refusal.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q11/p1", "position": "Fear of God's punishment restrains him from murder and urges Cain to fear God too.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī names punishment for killing; al-Ṭabrisī, al-Nasafī, al-Muqātil and Elmalılı connect fear with refusal. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī connects fear with divine recompense and piety, and says God affirms Abel's piety by repeating his words without correction."}, {"id": "5:28/q11/p2", "position": "His fear reveals knowledge of God.", "reasons": "Al-Qāshānī cites 35:28, that the learned truly fear God. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī cites 35:28 and 18:65; God's uncorrected quotation affirms the speaker's knowledge."}, {"id": "5:28/q11/p3", "position": "The clause gives the cause of the preceding refusal.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr says the separated clause beginning with inna signals this causal explanation."}, {"id": "5:28/q11/p4", "position": "Fear recalls God's perfection and care for what He created.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī links divine perfection and the title Lord of the worlds to refusing to destroy God's work."}]}
{"id": "5:28/q12", "question": "What does 'Lord of the worlds' add?", "turns_on": "Whether the title chiefly evokes sovereign punishment or care for creation.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q12/p1", "position": "God owns all creatures and can punish the killer.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī explains the title as owner of every creature, with power to punish wrongful killing."}, {"id": "5:28/q12/p2", "position": "It recalls God's creating and nurturing all, making murder a destruction of His work.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī connects lordship with beneficence and nurturing."}]}
{"id": "5:28/q13", "question": "How was Abel killed, and what preceded the murder?", "turns_on": "Whether murder occurred by surprise or through Abel's conscious surrender; the accounts also differ in their surrounding details.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q13/p1", "position": "Cain killed him treacherously while he slept, striking his head with a large stone.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī and later sources use the sleeping report to challenge an inference of chosen nonresistance. {"id": "5:28/q15", "question": "How should the reports urging imitation of Abel during civil strife be understood?", "turns_on": "The fitna setting, the parties' intentions, and the reliability of surrender reports.", "positions": [{"id": "5:28/q15/p1", "position": "They counsel abstention from escalating fighting, even when threatened.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī reports the Prophet's instruction to Saʿd to be like Adam's better son. {"id": "5:30/q08", "question": "How did Cain kill Abel?", "turns_on": "Reports differ in weapon, setting and Abel's conduct.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q08/p1", "position": "He used stones after Satan demonstrated crushing a bird or animal's head.", "reasons": "Ibn Jurayj and Mujāhid report ignorance of how to kill; Iblīs appears as a bird in some versions. Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd and others agree broadly; Study Quran calls this the common report."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p3", "position": "Abel submitted during the attack.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī, Bursevī and Ālūsī preserve the detail."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p4", "position": "The verse establishes the killing but no definite method.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī allows variant methods without deciding; Abū Ḥayyān says the verse omits the method."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p5", "position": "He pelted Abel with stones.", "reasons": "Ibn al-Jawzī cites Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p6", "position": "He used an iron implement.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr attributes this to Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p7", "position": "He strangled and bit Abel like a predatory beast.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr attributes this to some People of the Book."}, {"id": "5:30/q08/p8", "position": "He stalked and killed by stealth.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers Abū Jaʿfar's account as better fitting reflection; Abel did not enable the attack."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q09", "question": "Did Cain already know a method of killing?", "turns_on": "Whether the satanic demonstration supplies the very concept of killing or a method.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q09/p1", "position": "No; Iblīs taught him by crushing a creature's head.", "reasons": "Ibn Jurayj and Mujāhid report a bird or other animal, sometimes with Iblīs as a bird."}, {"id": "5:30/q09/p2", "position": "He grasped that life could be ended; uncertainty concerned the method.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī reports intuitive knowledge; Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the prior threat makes literal ignorance inconsistent, so the report may mean choosing a method."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q10", "question": "Where was Abel killed?", "turns_on": "Reports name mutually different places and the verse names none.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q10/p1", "position": "Near the pass at Ḥirāʾ.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī is named by Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī; others preserve the site as an alternative."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p2", "position": "In Basra at the future Great Mosque.", "reasons": "Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is cited by al-Thaʿlabī, Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī; others repeat the site."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p3", "position": "On Mount Thawr or Nawd near Mecca.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for Nawd, Thawr, and a 'mountain bull' in Mecca; Bursevī lists Thawr."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p4", "position": "On Mount Qāsiyūn in Damascus.", "reasons": "Al-Durr transmits a Prophetic report; Ṭabāṭabāʾī deems it acceptable. Kaʿb points to a blood streak, though Ṭabāṭabāʾī doubts the physical trace."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p5", "position": "On Mount Dayr al-Murrān.", "reasons": "Kaʿb identified a blood streak there as the murder's sign; Ālūsī repeats the report. Ṭabāṭabāʾī questions the trace."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p6", "position": "In India.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī places a stone-killing there; Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam found Abel's body there."}, {"id": "5:30/q10/p7", "position": "The verse provides no location.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān notes it omits the disputed place; al-Ṭabarī limits certainty to the killing."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q11", "question": "How old was Abel when killed?", "turns_on": "Whether the age report is accepted.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q11/p1", "position": "Twenty years old.", "reasons": "Ibn Jurayj and later commentators transmit twenty, often beside the Ḥirāʾ and Basra reports."}, {"id": "5:30/q11/p2", "position": "The verse gives no age.", "reasons": "Abū Ḥayyān says the age is among disputed extra-Qur'anic details."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q12", "question": "Was Abel the first human killed?", "turns_on": "The first-killing claim derives from reports.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q12/p1", "position": "Yes; Cain first instituted murder.", "reasons": "Al-Māwardī, Jishumī and al-Ṭabrisī give the claim, reinforced by the Prophetic inherited-guilt reports."}, {"id": "5:30/q12/p2", "position": "The verse establishes only Abel's murder.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī treats the killing as certain without settling narrative detail."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q13", "question": "What happened to Abel's body?", "turns_on": "The body is variously left, carried or buried after a raven's lesson.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q13/p1", "position": "Cain left it exposed, sometimes after stripping it.", "reasons": "Al-Suddī reports exposure; al-Zajjāj adds stripping and a desolate plain; Ālūsī says Cain did not know burial."}, {"id": "5:30/q13/p2", "position": "A raven taught Cain burial.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī and al-Durr describe one raven killing and burying another; Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this illustrates learning through observation."}, {"id": "5:30/q13/p3", "position": "He carried it in a sack.", "reasons": "Al-Wāḥidī says Cain did not know what to do with the first corpse

{"id": "5:30/q14", "question": "What followed the killing in Adam's family and nature?", "turns_on": "The reports offer differing consequences and incompatible dates for Seth.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q14/p1", "position": "Adam mourned for a century or ceased laughing.", "reasons": "Salim reports a hundred-year mourning; another account has an angel explain bayyaka as 'make you laugh'. Study Quran reports he never laughed again. Ibn Kathīr reports Ḥawwāʾ's first wailing."}, {"id": "5:30/q14/p2", "position": "The earth drank Abel's blood and was cursed thereafter.", "reasons": "Reports vary on whether God, Adam or Cain uttered the curse; al-Awzāʿī adds seven days of earthquakes and blood crying."}, {"id": "5:30/q14/p3", "position": "Seth replaced Abel.", "reasons": "Salim says Seth, 'God's gift', was born when Adam was 130, five years after murder; Muhyī al-Sunna says fifty years later, adds fifty scriptures, and says Seth inherited Adam. Other reports describe his instruction in worship."}, {"id": "5:30/q14/p4", "position": "Cain's white body blackened and Adam questioned him.", "reasons": "Al-Baghawī, Rāzī and Ālūsī give the darkening; some include Cain's denial and Adam's grief."}, {"id": "5:30/q14/p5", "position": "Vegetation, food, fruit, water, earth and animal behavior changed.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās describes the environmental changes; Muqātil says formerly tame animals and birds fled."}, {"id": "5:30/q14/p6", "position": "Iblīs mocked Adam's lament in verse.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī preserves the poem blaming Iblīs's schemes for Paradise's loss."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q15", "question": "Did Adam compose the reported elegy?", "turns_on": "Authenticity and original language of the elegy.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q15/p1", "position": "Adam lamented in verses about a changed, dusty land.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī continues the elegy to Abel's burial. Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Qurṭubī transmit it; the latter notes the accusative bashāsha. Ālūsī cites ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās transmissions."}, {"id": "5:30/q15/p2", "position": "Adam lamented in Syriac; Yaʿrub later made it Arabic verse.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās denies Adam composed Arabic poetry, citing 36:69; the lament passed through Seth to Yaʿrub, who ordered or translated it into meter."}, {"id": "5:30/q15/p3", "position": "The poem is forged or too defective to attribute to Adam.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī and Rāzī cite its poor quality and Adam's God-given knowledge; Ālūsī lists grammatical and rhyme defects. Ṭabāṭabāʾī doubts related reports."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q16", "question": "Does the first murderer share guilt for later murders?", "turns_on": "How founding a practice and repentance affect liability.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q16/p1", "position": "Yes; each unjust killing adds a share because he instituted murder.", "reasons": "Many sources cite the Prophet; Ibn Kathīr notes broad hadith transmission, al-Qurṭubī cites Muslim. Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī also names Satan. ʿAlī links Cain and Iblīs to 41:29."}, {"id": "5:30/q16/p2", "position": "Founding any good or bad practice carries followers' reward or burden.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī and al-Qurṭubī cite the Prophetic maxim; al-Qurṭubī applies it to Iblīs, innovators and misleading leaders. Ālūsī suggests Cain bears later fire-worship guilt."}, {"id": "5:30/q16/p3", "position": "Repentance or forgetfulness prevents inherited liability.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī says Adam repented and was forgiven, and prefers that his eating was forgetful, hence not sinful; he points to his Baqara discussion."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q17", "question": "On what day is the murder reported to have happened?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q17/p1", "position": "Tuesday.", "reasons": "A report from Anas has the Prophet call Tuesday a day of blood because Eve menstruated and Adam's son killed his brother then."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q18", "question": "Does aṣbaḥa date the murder?", "turns_on": "General change of state versus a literal time reference.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q18/p1", "position": "It means 'became' and fixes no time of day.", "reasons": "Al-Ḍamghānī cites 18:45 and 3:103; Abū Ḥayyān says several time verbs generalized to ṣāra. Al-Ṭabrisī, Ālūsī and Ṭabāṭabāʾī reject the night inference."}, {"id": "5:30/q18/p2", "position": "Morning evokes the beginning of a continuing state or expected relief.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites al-Rabīʿ ibn Ḍabʿ and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ for continuing use; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the rationale. Al-Biqāʿī says morning normally promises relief."}, {"id": "5:30/q18/p3", "position": "It implies Cain killed at night.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabrisī and Ṭabāṭabāʾī report the inference, then reject it."}, {"id": "5:30/q18/p4", "position": "It may retain literal morning, when murder occurred.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr pairs this alternative with Cain's visible worldly misery."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q19", "question": "What happened to Cain later?", "turns_on": "Reports describe distinct later fates and origins.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q19/p1", "position": "He fled to Aden and instituted fire worship after Satan deceived him.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī adds fugitive status and his sister Hibat Allāh; several sources say Satan misexplained the accepted offering as fire worship."}, {"id": "5:30/q19/p2", "position": "God removed his reason or heart and he wandered until death.", "reasons": "ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Faḍāla gives this report."}, {"id": "5:30/q19/p3", "position": "A blind grandson accidentally killed him with a stone.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī says the grandson then killed his accusing son with a slap."}, {"id": "5:30/q19/p4", "position": "His descendants fell into vice and perished in Noah's flood.", "reasons": "Al-Thaʿlabī lists instruments, wine, fire worship and adultery."}, {"id": "5:30/q19/p5", "position": "His conception came from a poisonous remnant of Adam's vomit.", "reasons": "Bursevī cites a master: the same tree made a snake deadly, and Cain a corrupter."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q20", "question": "What was Cain's loss?", "turns_on": "Worldly, moral, spiritual and otherworldly scopes of loss.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q20/p1", "position": "Loss in this world and the next.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās specifies parents' anger and brotherlessness here, God's wrath and Hell hereafter. Al-Bayḍāwī adds exile; Bursevī and Elmalılı say loss of religion and worldly life."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p2", "position": "Loss of good deeds.", "reasons": "Al-Zajjāj's gloss recurs in Ibn al-Jawzī, al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p3", "position": "Worldly agony, agitation or disappointment.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿĀshūr connects it with a morning reading; Ibn ʿAṭiyya conditionally includes Mujāhid's torment account."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p4", "position": "He simply became one of the losers.", "reasons": "Muqātil and al-Nasafī leave it general; Ālūsī says the plural 'one of' intensifies the point."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p5", "position": "Loss of the afterlife through a bad bargain.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī says he sold the afterlife for worldly life; Ibn ʿĀshūr gives an otherworldly reading."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p6", "position": "Destruction of his own self.", "reasons": "Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā's gloss is transmitted by Ibn al-Jawzī and Abū Ḥayyān."}, {"id": "5:30/q20/p7", "position": "God and other humans grew angry with him.", "reasons": "Al-Biqāʿī connects it to assaulting God's creation and a fellow human."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q21", "question": "Was Cain an unbeliever or a sinner?", "turns_on": "How the reports bear on Cain's faith.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q21/p1", "position": "He was an unbeliever, at least at death.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās calls him unbelieving; Ālūsī infers this from reports of his wretched end. Al-Māwardī notes this view."}, {"id": "5:30/q21/p2", "position": "He was a grave sinner rather than an unbeliever.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers this as the apparent reading; al-Māwardī records it."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q22", "question": "What punishment is reported for Cain?", "turns_on": "Conflicting bodily scenes, places and durations.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q22/p1", "position": "A fixed leg, sun-facing fire in summer and ice in winter.", "reasons": "Mujāhid's account differs on which leg and duration; Ṭabāṭabāʾī adds seven angels. Ibn ʿAṭiyya conditions its relevance on authenticity."}, {"id": "5:30/q22/p2", "position": "Half the punishment of Hell's inhabitants.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿUmar or ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr are cited; some say equal sharing."}, {"id": "5:30/q22/p3", "position": "He is Hell's most wretched, bearing later bloodshed.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAmr calls him most wretched; a Prophetic report lists him among three such people."}, {"id": "5:30/q22/p4", "position": "He hangs upside down, unable to reach water.", "reasons": "One report gives a dead town and pool; another a sea island until resurrection."}, {"id": "5:30/q22/p5", "position": "He hangs by his horns in the sun until resurrection.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī lists this among reports he regards as weak or corrupted."}]}

{"id": "5:30/q24", "question": "What other verses illuminate this account?", "turns_on": "Different cross-references serve different points.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q24/p1", "position": "The killing leads to 5:32 and recalls the warning of 4:93.", "reasons": "Mujāhid connects both passages."}, {"id": "5:30/q24/p2", "position": "Cain and Iblīs are the two misleaders in 41:29.", "reasons": "ʿAlī gives this identification."}, {"id": "5:30/q24/p3", "position": "The evil soul parallels Joseph's statement in 12:53.", "reasons": "Study Quran cites Joseph."}, {"id": "5:30/q24/p4", "position": "Ṭawwaʿat is stronger than sawwalat in 20:96 and 12:18.", "reasons": "Samarrāʾī says murder required greater effort to overcome resistance."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q25", "question": "How is the murder read inwardly?", "turns_on": "Which inner faculties and losses the figures portray.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q25/p1", "position": "The lower self kills the heart and loses spiritual goods in both worlds.", "reasons": "Bursevī identifies Cain with self and Abel with heart, listing lost unveiling, gnosis, intimacy, gardens and divine vision and citing 103:1–2. Qāshānī says estimation suppresses intellect and stirs greed and animal pleasure."}, {"id": "5:30/q25/p2", "position": "Inward corruption is punished in spiritual perception.", "reasons": "Al-Qushayrī distinguishes outward legal punishment from inward loss of inspiration, gnosis, intimacy and worship."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q26", "question": "How do the Qur'an and Torah accounts compare?", "turns_on": "Authority of extra-Qur'anic reports and the portrayal of God.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q26/p1", "position": "The Qur'an teaches human learning without the Torah's anthropomorphic God.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī compares Genesis 4's offerings, mark, curse and departure to Nod; he rejects its picture of God as an earthly person who withdraws or hides. The raven shows gradual learning."}, {"id": "5:30/q26/p2", "position": "Traditional names and extra-Qur'anic details have uncertain authority.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī contrasts Qābīl with Torah Qayin, questions the Torah chain and altered text, notes related reports in Sunni and Shiʿi routes, and rejects many as weak or corrupt."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q27", "question": "What became of Abel's accepted offering?", "turns_on": "The reports disagree on whether the ram replaced Isaac or Ishmael.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q27/p1", "position": "The ram became the ransom sacrificed in place of Isaac.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAbbās's account in al-Ṭabarī includes twin births, a marriage dispute, the two offerings, and the end of sibling marriage after four generations."}, {"id": "5:30/q27/p2", "position": "The ram was kept in Paradise forty years before replacing Ishmael.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī reports this distinct version."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q28", "question": "What does the corpse's saw'ah signify in the related burial account?", "turns_on": "Whether the term names exposed private parts or the whole body.", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q28/p1", "position": "The genitals.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī transmits this gloss."}, {"id": "5:30/q28/p2", "position": "The murdered man's corpse.", "reasons": "Al-Qurṭubī gives this alternative."}]}
{"id": "5:30/q29", "question": "What other benefits followed the introduction of death?", "turns_on": "", "positions": [{"id": "5:30/q29/p1", "position": "Wind enabled burial and death in old age eased weariness.", "reasons": "A report from Anas names three benefits: wind so relatives could bury their dead, worms in grain so rulers would not hoard it as money, and death after old age to ease families' burden."}]}
{"id": "5:55/q01", "question": "What does innamā restrict?", "turns_on": "Whether restriction is exhaustive, and whether its object is support or governing authority.", "positions": [{"id": "5:55/q01/p1", "position": "It confines the stated guardianship to God, the Messenger, and the described believers.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī calls the restriction obligatory; al-Ṭabrisī gives the dirham, Ḥātim, and al-Aʿshā examples; Ibn ʿĀshūr says the affirmative report acts as a command to maintain allegiance; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers qasr al-ifrād against imagined additional guardians, while allowing qasr al-qalb."}, {"id": "5:55/q01/p2", "position": "The particle need not exclude every other description or restrict walī to authority.", "reasons": "Al-Rāzī cites 10:24 and 47:36, where the descriptions of worldly life are not exhaustive; he says even restricted named allies can be a particular supporting group."}]}
{"id": "5:55/q02", "question": "How is the main sentence constructed?", "turns_on": "How the singular predicate relates grammatically to the coordinated names.", "positions": [{"id": "5:55/q02/p1", "position": "The sentence is nominal, with God as predicate and Messenger and believers coordinated with Him.", "reasons": "Al-Naḥḥās and al-Samīn give this parse; al-Burhān calls coordination with God a mode of magnification, comparing 3:18 and 4:69; Qāshānī sees an inward unity then outward distinction, comparing 3:18."}, {"id": "5:55/q02/p2", "position": "The later names may be understood through an implicit 'likewise' or a plural predicate.", "reasons": "Al-Ālūsī says either parse shows the Messenger and believers become allies by God's appointment."}]}
{"id": "5:55/q03", "question": "What does walī mean here?", "turns_on": "Whether walī denotes mutual support or delegated authority, and whether one use can carry multiple senses.", "positions": [{"id": "5:55/q03/p1", "position": "A religious ally, friend, protector, or helper who gives support and mutual loyalty.", "reasons": "Al-Ṭabarī excludes Jewish and Christian allies; al-Rāzī invokes 5:51, 5:54, and 5:57, contemporaneous support and affection, and the rule against combining homonymous senses; al-Ālūsī says the verse consoles believers and its opponents were never imams; 9:71 confirms mutual allegiance. Al-Rāghib derives the senses from proximity; al-Dāmghānī calls it religious allegiance."}, {"id": "5:55/q03/p2", "position": "One entitled to manage affairs and owed obedience, with divine authority delegated to the Messenger and the identified believer.", "reasons": "Al-Mubarrad defines the root as awlā; al-Kumayt uses walī al-amr for a successor. Al-Ṭabrisī cites marriage guardians, blood claimants, rulers, and heirs and says ordinary mutual friendship cannot be exclusive under 9:71. The Shīʿī argument cites the marriage-guardian usage and the shared singular walī; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī derives wilāya from proximity, distinguishes ontological and legislative authority, and cites 33:6, 4:59, and 33:36 for the Prophet's delegated governance. Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says believers support God or the Messenger in the Qurʾan (61:14, 47:7, 3:81, 7:157, 59:8, 8:72), while the Prophet shares religious distinction with them and is never called their supporter in that sense."}, {"id": "5:55/q03/p3", "position": "Walī has a broad family of senses rooted in nearness, including protection, affection, aid, and management.", "reasons": "Al-Rāghib traces walāʾ and tawālī from spatial succession to kinship, faith, affection, support and taking charge; al-Ṭabrisī and Ibn al-Jawzī enumerate concrete holders of protective or managing rights; Elmalılı uses guardians, authorities, friends and helpers together. Al-Rāghib observes tawallā with a direct object means turning toward, but with ʿan means turning away (2:144); al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī applies the idiom to battle and course."}, {"id": "5:55/q03/p4", "position": "The verse can convey support and authority together.", "reasons": "The reported Shīʿī reasoning allows the senses to coexist; Elmalılı lists both, while al-Rāzī says a single homonymous expression cannot carry both at once."}]}
{"id": "5:55/q04", "question": "Why is walī singular for several guardians?", "turns_on": "Whether the singular marks divine priority or follows generic and morphological usage.", "positions": [{"id": "5:55/q04/p1", "position": "God is the original guardian; the Messenger and believers share that role derivatively.", "reasons": "Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Rāzī, al-Nasafī, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Ālūsī, al-Biqāʿī and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī say the plural would hide the priority; al-Ālūsī offers an implied 'likewise' or plural predicate as syntactic explanations and stresses that conjunction does not equate rank."}, {"id": "5:55/q04/p2", "position": "Walī is a generic noun or a faʿīl form usable for singular or plural.", "reasons": "Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Abū Ḥayyān call it generic; al-Samīn notes faʿīl's invariant form and cites 11:89 by analogy.
